This guide explains ksTFL styling primitives (`s_*` helpers), how to create and apply named styles with `add_style()`, and how style combinations created with `f_combine()` are resolved during `create_report()`.

Package-provided styles: ksTFL also ships a set of predefined style templates (clinical defaults) that you can reference by name in `labelStyleRef`, `valueStyleRef` or `styleRef`. These built-in templates provide sensible defaults for fonts, paragraph spacing and table presentation and may be used directly or combined with your custom styles via `f_combine()` to create more complex styling.

1) Style primitives (what they do)

- `s_font(...)` — font family, `font_size` (with units, e.g. "12pt"), `bold`, `italic`, `underline`, `color` (hex or name), `highlight` (background color).
- `s_paragraph(...)` — paragraph-level settings: `alignment` (left/right/center/justify/distributed), `spacing` (use `s_spacing()`), `indents` (use `s_indents()`), `word_style` (Word style name).
- `s_spacing(before, after, line_spacing)` — nested helper for paragraph spacing; accepts units like "6pt" and `line_spacing` multiplier (>= 1).
- `s_indents(left, right, first_line)` — nested helper for indents; accepts units like "10mm" or negative for hanging.
- `s_table_style(...)` — cell-level styling: `background_color`, `row_height` (e.g. "15mm" or "auto"), `vertical_alignment` (top/center/bottom), `text_orientation` (horizontal, vertical_90, vertical_270), `borders` (use `s_borders()`).
- `s_borders(...)` and `s_border(color, width, line_style)` — define per-side border properties; `line_style` must be one of `single`, `double`, `dashed`, `dotted`, `thick`, `none` and `width` requires units like "1pt".

2) Declaring styles: `add_style()`

Call `add_style(spec, id, ...)` to create or update a named style in `spec$attribs$styles`.

- Each modifier (e.g., `s_font(...)`) is mapped to a schema path (font, paragraph, table_style) and validated against allowed properties.
- Multiple calls to `add_style()` with the same `id` merge using a last-win strategy (fields in later calls override or extend earlier ones).

Example — create a named style and a numeric alignment style:

```r
spec <- create_table(mtcars)
spec <- spec |> 
  add_style("title_header_style",
    s_font(font_name = "Arial", font_size = "12pt", bold = TRUE),
    s_paragraph(alignment = "center", spacing = s_spacing(before = "6pt", after = "6pt")),
    s_table_style(background_color = "#F2F2F2")
  ) |> 
  add_style("numeric_right", s_paragraph(alignment = "right"))
```

Note: header/footer rendering is governed by the Word document template. ksTFL stores header/footer rows as content only; it does not maintain a separate header/footer style store inside the spec. If you need to override a template header/footer style you must create a named style whose id matches the style name used by your template (see `inst/schemas/styles_schema_v0.json`). This is an advanced, template-dependent mechanism — for most workflows apply named styles to titles, subtitles, footnotes and table cells.

3) Applying styles

- Text groups (`add_title`, `add_subtitle`, `add_footnote`, `add_body_text`) accept `styleRef` — a character vector of style names or a single style name.
- Columns accept `labelStyleRef` and `valueStyleRef` when using `define_cols()`.

Example — apply styles to columns and titles:

```r
spec <- spec |> 
  define_cols(c(mpg, hp), labelStyleRef = "header_style", valueStyleRef = "numeric_right") |> 
  add_title("Demographics", styleRef = "header_style")
```

4) Combining styles with `f_combine()` — why and how

Why combine styles?

- Often you want to apply more than one named style to the same element (e.g., `bold` + `color_red` + `border_bottom`). Rather than duplicating combined definitions, you can reference multiple styles and let ksTFL merge them into one final style.

How `f_combine()` works

- `f_combine("styleA", "styleB")` simply returns a character vector of style names. It is a convenience to explicitly indicate multiple style names that should be applied together.
At the `create_report()` stage, ksTFL scans the spec for style references that are length > 1 (combinations). It sorts the names (so order does not matter), computes a unique hash for the sorted combination, merges the component style definitions using the package's internal recursive-merge logic (last-win across component styles in the sorted order), and writes the merged style into `spec$attribs$styles` under the generated hash name (e.g., `style_<hash>`).

Key consequences:

- The combination is order-independent (because ksTFL sorts the component names before hashing), avoiding accidental duplicate merged styles caused by different argument ordering.
- After `create_report()`, all elements will reference the single merged style name (the computed hash), making downstream renderers simpler.

Example — combine label emphasis and a color:

```r
spec <- spec |> 
  add_style("bold_em", s_font(bold = TRUE)) |> 
  add_style("red", s_font(color = "#FF0000")) |> 
  define_cols("age", labelStyleRef = f_combine("bold_em", "red"))

# When creating report: create_report(spec) -> merged style created and applied automatically
```

5) Practical rules and validation notes

- Do not call `s_*` helper functions outside of `add_style()` (they assert context and will error otherwise).
- Allowed values: font names (examples: Arial, Courier New, Times New Roman, Calibri), alignments (left, right, center, justify, distributed), border styles (single, double, dashed, dotted, thick, none). The package stores these enumerations as internal constants; the vignette lists the accepted values explicitly above so you do not need to reference internal symbols.
- If you want to modify global defaults, use `tfl_set_options(add_style(...))` to set styles in the package options — these session defaults are applied automatically when a spec is initialized.

6) Troubleshooting

- If you see an error about unknown parameters in a modifier, check the allowed property names in the documentation for the corresponding `s_*` helper (for example `font_name`, `font_size`, `background_color`). The package validates modifiers against the schema internally; the vignette lists the accepted parameters and common allowed values above.
- If combined styles are not appearing as expected, ensure you call `create_report()` — consolidation of combinations happens there.

7) Reference: allowed values and patterns

Below are the exact allowed enumerations and common validation patterns used by ksTFL (sourced from the package constants). Use these values when supplying arguments to `s_*` helpers or `define_cols()`.

- Font names (`s_font(font_name)`):
  - Arial, Courier New, Times New Roman, Calibri
- Text alignment (`s_paragraph(alignment)`):
  - left, right, center, justify, distributed
- Border line styles (`s_border(line_style)`):
  - single, double, dashed, dotted, thick, none
- Vertical alignment (`s_table_style(vertical_alignment)`):
  - top, center, bottom
- Text orientation (`s_table_style(text_orientation)`):
  - horizontal, vertical_90, vertical_270
- Page sizes (`p_page(size)`):
  - A4, A3, Letter, Legal, Executive
- Page orientations (`p_page(orientation)`):
  - portrait, landscape
- Column types (detected by the package's column-format logic, and used by `define_cols(type)`):
  - string, numeric

Validation patterns (use when constructing values):

- Font size: must include units, e.g. `12pt` (pattern: numeric + `pt`).
- Hex color: `#RRGGBB` (6 hex digits). Color names from ksTFL color map are also accepted (e.g., `red`, `blue`, `grey20`).
- Spacing and indents: units allowed `pt`, `cm`, `in`, `mm` (e.g., `6pt`, `10mm`).
- Border width: points only, e.g. `1pt`, `2pt`.
- Column width and content width: percentages or units: `25%`, `3.5cm`, `1in`.

Use these exact tokens — the package validates inputs and will raise informative errors when values are not in the allowed set or fail pattern checks.

End of Styling Guide.
